propositions: The ticket originally sought a shared reconcile_one function to eliminate duplication between sync.reconverge and s3_doctor._fold_heads, but Gerrit 1665 removed the doctor's worktree merge, making the targeted duplication obsolete.

Sync and the doctor hold contradictory unrelated-history policies: sync refuses to merge when the local store carries events (anti-graft rule), while the doctor unions unconditionally and is pinned by a held-out test.
Sync cannot adopt the doctor's ref-only merge engine because its consumers read ticket events from the tracker's worktree files, while a ref-only merge would leave readers seeing pre-merge state.
The two healers have fundamentally opposed failure policies: sync must never raise, while the doctor must raise to allow the push path to abandon.

A behaviour-preserving shared reconcile_one cannot be implemented without safety-critical policy flags, so the ticket is closed as obsolete with rejected alternatives (thin extraction and deep unification) documented.
